ShouldFlush.rationale: The predicate itself was never in doubt (runic_pyramid.py:16-17 returns False unconditionally = RunicPyramid.cs's ShouldFlush for the owner). The recorded divergence was in the CONSUMER: combat.py used to gate the whole discard_hand call on the predicate and so skipped the tail. Today combat.py:1793 calls `self.player.discard_hand(flush=self.hooks.should_flush_hand())` unconditionally, and player.discard_hand (player.py:420-467) mirrors CombatManager.cs:1313-1347 -- with flush=False `flushed` is empty (player.py:461) and the hand is left intact, but the tail (`self.end_of_turn_cleanup()`, player.py:467) still runs regardless. RE-READ 2026-08-04: the Joss Paper witness this entry originally cited is now STALE in a different way than the 2026-07-28 reconciliation described -- Joss Paper no longer hangs its deferred Ethereal credit off `on_hand_emptied`/the flush tail at all (that hook does not even exist on discard_hand any more, per player.py's own docstring: 'No on_hand_emptied here either ... the flush is the one site the sim used to fire it from (turn_structure G16)'). relics/joss_paper.py's credit is on `after_player_turn_end` (joss_paper.py:53-66), dispatched from combat.py:1796 -- AFTER discard_hand (combat.py:1793) unconditionally, exactly matching JossPaper.cs:116-124's AfterSideTurnEnd, which C# also fires unconditionally after FlushPlayerHand regardless of ShouldFlush's outcome. So Runic Pyramid's ShouldFlush=False no longer interacts with Joss Paper's credit AT ALL in the current sim, on either side -- which is MORE faithful than the previous witness implied (the two relics were never supposed to interact through the flush tail; C# credits Joss Paper from a wholly separate post-flush hook). The mechanism this hook governs (does a false ShouldFlush still let the turn-end tail run) remains faithful on its own terms via end_of_turn_cleanup, independent of Joss Paper. RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: Rollup of guards G1 and N1 per binding rule 4. The predicate itself is faithful -- the sim returns False unconditionally, matching RunicPyramid.cs:10-17 for the owner -- but the sim's CONSUMER of the predicate diverges: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 61 and guard G4 record that C#'s FlushPlayerHand treats ShouldFlush == false as 'retain every card' and still runs Hook.AfterFlush and PlayerCombatState.EndOfTurnCleanup (CombatManager.cs:1327-1346), while combat.py:661-662 gates the whole discard_hand call on the predicate and so skips the tail as well. That record labels the mechanism a LIVE gap and names relics/runic_pyramid.py:16-17 as one of its two ported witnesses; binding rule 3 -- one verdict per mechanism -- so this entry cites and matches it rather than re-deriving it. Rule 7: turn_structure.json, CombatManager.cs, combat.py, hooks.py and relics/joss_paper.py are NOT hashed by this record; the seam record hashes the machinery.
